accuracy.evidence: The three steps follow Bruner (1966) enactive, iconic and symbolic modes and the NCETM concrete-pictorial-abstract approach; the advice to link objects and drawings to the symbols, and to fade them, is EEF (2017) KS2-3 maths recommendation 2 and EEF (2020) EYFS-KS1 guidance. Division by sharing with materials and the ÷ and = signs is NC Year 2. The adult text notes that 12 ÷ 3 can also be read as grouping (how many 3s in 12), so the lab's 'the 3 is the plates' is tied to the sharing story, and every prediction and challenge item about what a number stands for names its story (plates, bags). Sums checked: 12 ÷ 3 = 4, 15 ÷ 5 = 3, 20 ÷ 4 = 5, 10 ÷ 2 = 5, 8 ÷ 2 = 4; parameterised items checked at corners (g, e from 2 to 5: g*e ÷ g = e is always a whole number).

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the documented slips: starting with the symbols (prediction 1, challenge 'symfirst'), objects are babyish or only for children who are behind (prediction 4, challenge 'babyish'), a drawing must look real (prediction 2, the slow strawberry drawing refused as the quick one), unequal groups that use all 12 (the fairness rule refuses giving to a plate that already has more, the 5-4-3 drawing is refused, Mia's 5, 4, 3 challenge), reading ÷ as − or × (12 − 3 = 9 and × refused in the sentence builder with their own reasons), writing 3 ÷ 12, confusing the 3 groups with 3 in each group (prediction 3, 'each' slip), and guessing, giving up or copying instead of going back a step.

lab_distinct.evidence: flagcpa walks one idea through three representations in order and then forces a step back: real strawberries dealt one at a time onto plates with a fairness rule, a choice between four ring drawings and then between a slow realistic drawing and quick dots, a left-to-right sentence builder for 12 ÷ 3 = 4, a link scene where each number is dragged onto its meaning in the plates story (with a 'left over' distractor), and a go-back scene for 15 ÷ 5. It is not 591 flagrepass or 683 (representing addition and numbers) or 695 flagbarm (bar models); the 6-token shingle gate reports no flag lab above 30%.

lab_teaches.evidence: The learner meets the idea by doing it first: dealing the strawberries shows 4 on each plate before any symbol appears; the drawing scene shows that dots in rings carry the same groups; the sentence builder then writes what was already done; the link scene makes each number point back to plates, strawberries and one plate; and in the last scene the only way forward for Zak is to go back a step and draw 15 dots in 5 rings, then read 3 off one ring. DONE lines confirm each step.

predictions.evidence: Four predictions with tempting wrong options the lab disproves: 'Look hard at the symbols' (the scene starts with moving strawberries and the answer is seen on the plates), 'Yes, draw them well' (the realistic drawing is refused as the quick one; dots show the same groups), '3 strawberries on each plate' (each plate has 4; the 3 tile goes in the groups box and links to The plates), and 'Yes, big kids only use symbols' (going back to dots is the step that solves 15 ÷ 5).

challenge_feedback.evidence: Seven questions; every wrong option maps to a named slip, checked with chal.cjs and fixed after the first click-through showed three mismatches (the fairness slip, the 4-groups-of-3 slip and the 'both are right' drawing slip were reused out of context): now 'guess', 'symfirst', 'swap2' (5 groups of 2, but 2 plates), 'unequal', 'each' (in this story the 4 is the bags), 'leftover', 'babyish', 'neat2' and 'minus'.

readability.evidence: Kid paragraphs are short sentences built around one concrete example (12 strawberries, 3 plates, 4 each) and stay inside the family kid limit; the adult text names Bruner, NCETM, EEF and NC Year 2 in plain words inside the adult limit (validators pass). Canvas text is one heading per scene and short labels such as '3 rings of 4' and 'Strawberries on one plate'.

no_filler.evidence: Kid paragraphs: step 1 real things, step 2 a quick picture, step 3 symbols with what each number means, and going back a step. Adult paragraphs: research and curriculum basis, how the lab uses sharing and the grouping caveat, named common mistakes plus fading, and what to do at home. The content gate finds no filler phrase.

mobile.evidence: Checked 360 px phone screenshots in light and dark for every scene and after Show me: 12 strawberries in two rows above three plates with counts, four ring drawings in a 2 x 2 grid (the no-rings dots were shrunk after the first screenshot showed them touching), the four sentence boxes with = and seven tiles in two rows above the reference drawing, the link scene's number tile above four picture cards, and five rings across the width in the go-back scene. Real mouse drags (strawberry to plate, tile to box, number to card, pen to ring) worked at 390 px.

accessibility.evidence: Every canvas action has a labelled button twin: 'Plate 1' ('Put a strawberry on plate 1'), one button per drawing, 'Strawberries with leaves' / 'Dots in rings', a button per tile ('Put ÷ in box 2'), a button per meaning ('12 stands for: All the strawberries'), the four stuck options, 'Ring 1' to 'Ring 5' and the answer buttons. The canvas aria-label carries the scene description and every piece of feedback, including each dot drawn (added after testing); challenge feedback is a role=status live region; axe (WCAG 2.1 AA) is clean in both themes in the browser gate.
